29 A diffraction grating experiment is set up using orange light of wavelength 600 nm. The grating
has a slit separation of 2.00 µm.

What is the angular separation (θ2 – θ1) between the first and second order maxima of the orange
light?
A
17.5°
B
19.4°
C
36.9°
D
54.3°

hints: Notice the diagram shows $\theta_1$ for 1st order and $\theta_2$ for 2nd order measured from the central dashed line, so you need both angles separately.
Recall the grating equation $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ with $d = 2.00\,\mu\text{m}$ and $\lambda = 600\,\text{nm}$ converted to the same metre units.
Calculate $\sin\theta_1 = \lambda/d$ for $n=1$ and $\sin\theta_2 = 2\lambda/d$ for $n=2$, take inverse sine for each, then subtract.
walkthrough: Write the grating condition for maxima: $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$, where $n=1$ for first order and $n=2$ for second order.
Find the angular separation: $\theta_2 - \theta_1 \approx 36.9^{\circ} - 17.5^{\circ} \approx 19.4^{\circ}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is $\theta_1$ alone from $\sin\theta_1 = \lambda/d = 0.3$, not the separation $\theta_2 - \theta_1$.

B.explanation: With $\theta_1 = 17.5^{\circ}$ and $\theta_2 = 36.9^{\circ}$, the difference is about $19.4^{\circ}$.

C.explanation: This is $\theta_2$ alone from $\sin\theta_2 = 2\lambda/d = 0.6$, not the separation between the two orders.

D.explanation: This is the sum $\theta_1 + \theta_2$, whereas the question asks for the difference $\theta_2 - \theta_1$.
